fields.Front: Give the full Week 2 definition of encapsulation.
fields.Back: Bundling data (attributes) and the methods that operate on them into a single unit or class, and restricting access to some of the object's components so its internal state is protected from direct access and modification by other objects.

fields.Text: The two key aspects of encapsulation are {{c1::data hiding}} (via access modifiers) and {{c2::getter and setter methods}}.

fields.Front: Why use getter and setter methods instead of direct access?
fields.Back: They allow additional validation or logic before changes are made, while keeping the public interface stable.

fields.Front: In the slide's Person class, what do getName() and setName() do?
fields.Back: getName() returns the private name; setName(string newName) assigns name = newName.

fields.Text: Benefits of encapsulation listed in Week 2: {{c1::security}}, {{c2::maintainability}}, and {{c3::reusability}}.
BankAccount's constructor sets balance to {{c1::0}} when the initial balance is negative.

fields.Front: Why does the slide's BankAccount have no setBalance() method?
fields.Back: So every change goes through deposit/withdraw, which validate; balance is read-only via getBalance().

fields.Text: In BankAccount, balance is {{c1::private}} and can only be accessed through the public methods {{c2::`getBalance`, `deposit`, `withdraw`}}.
